Manufacturers: Same as applicant ("Applicant and Manufacturer" label) — Rice Lake Weighing Systems. I'll include manufacturers as same entity since the label says "Applicant and Manufacturer".

Certified type:
- Category: "Multi-Dimensional Measuring instrument" — the schema examples include "Measuring system" etc. The document says "A Multi-Dimensional Measuring instrument". I'll use "Multi-dimensional measuring instrument".
- Type designations: iDimension LTL, iDimension LTL-XL, iDimension PWD, iDimension Flex

Model family: The cert covers 4 type designations: iDimension LTL, iDimension LTL-XL, iDimension PWD, iDimension Flex. But the characteristics tables don't vary per model — the characteristics are given per principle of operation (drop and clear vs stop and go), not per model. Hmm. The tables vary by configuration axis (principle of operation), not by model. So per rule 4, model_family should include models only if cert covers >1 model variant. The cert covers 4 type designations. The characteristics are not broken down per model — they are shared across all models, with differences per principle of operation.

I think I should include model_family with the 4 models (type designations), since the cert covers 4 variants. But do attributes vary per model? No — the tables don't differentiate. However the schema says "include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant" — the cert does cover 4 variants. So include:

"model_family": {
  "family_name": "iDimension",
  "models": [
    {"model_id": "iDimension LTL"},
    {"model_id": "iDimension LTL-XL"},
    {"model_id": "iDimension PWD"},
    {"model_id": "iDimension Flex"}
  ]
}

family_name: "iDimension" is the common prefix — is that an "explicit family name"? It's not explicitly stated as a family name. The types are listed as iDimension LTL etc. I could set family_name to null, or "iDimension". Being cautious, maybe null since not explicit. Actually "iDimension" is clearly the product family prefix but not explicitly named as a family. I'll use null to avoid fabrication. Hmm, but it might be helpful. Rule 8 says don't fabricate. I'll set family_name to null.

Characteristics:

The characteristics vary by "principle of operation" — that's a configuration axis. Two tables:

Table 1: Drop and clear (footnotes 1,3)
- Maximum dimension: Length max ≤ 360 cm, Width max ≤ 240 cm, Height max ≤ 240 cm
- Minimum dimension: min ≥ 20 cm (L, W, H all)
- Scale interval d: d ≥ 2 cm (L, W, H)

Table 2: Stop and go (footnotes 2,3)
- Maximum dimension: Length ≤ 180, Width ≤ 180, Height ≤ 210 cm
- Minimum dimension: min ≥ 30 cm
- Scale interval d: d ≥ 2 cm

Page 3 (type-level, applies to all):
- Principle of measurement: reflection of light
- Measuring range: Single interval
- Electromagnetic environment class: E2
- Mechanical environment class: M1
- Climatic environment:
  - temperature range: -10 °C / +40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit °C
  - humidity: non-condensing
  - intended location: Closed
- Power supply voltage: 100 – 240 V AC 50/60 Hz → split:
  - power_supply_voltage: {min: 100, max: 240}, V
  - power_supply_frequency: {min: 50, max: 60}, Hz
  - power_supply_type: AC
- Method of operation: semi-automatic or automatic
- Limitations of use: two entries
- Minimum spacing between successive objects: ≥ 35 cm (multiple objects simultaneously in the measurement area)
- Software identification: Version number 6.1.r.b with explanation

Configuration-level characteristics (axis = principle of operation):

config_level entries:
1. attribute: maximum_dimension, axis: principle_of_operation, values:
   - {condition: "drop and clear", dimension?...}

Hmm, this is a 2D matrix: principle of operation × dimension (length/width/height). How to encode? Options:
- One config_level entry per attribute-dimension combo, e.g. "maximum_dimension_length" with axis "principle_of_operation" and values for each condition.
- Or use matrix_tables to preserve the tables and config_level for the key ones.

I think the cleanest is:

config_level:
- attribute: "maximum_dimension_length", axis: "principle_of_operation", values: [{condition: "drop_and_clear", value: {min: null, max: 360}, unit_symbol: "cm", footnote_markers: ["1)", "3)"]}, {condition: "stop_and_go", value: {min: null, max: 180}, unit_symbol: "cm", footnote_markers: ["2)", "3)"]}]
- attribute: "maximum_dimension_width", ... drop_and_clear max 240; stop_and_go max 180
- attribute: "maximum_dimension_height", ... drop_and_clear max 240; stop_and_go max 210
- attribute: "minimum_dimension", axis: "principle_of_operation", values: [{condition: "drop_and_clear", value: {min: 20, max: null}, unit: "cm"}, {condition: "stop_and_go", value: {min: 30, max: null}, unit: "cm"}]
- attribute: "scale_interval", axis: "principle_of_operation", values: [{condition: "drop_and_clear", value: {min: 2, max: null}, unit: "cm"}, {condition: "stop_and_go", ... same}]

Wait, should maximum_dimension be split into length/width/height as separate attributes, or should the axis include dimension? The schema says config_level entries have attribute, axis, values[]: {condition, value}. Since max dimension has 3 sub-dimensions each varying, I'll make three attributes: maximum_dimension_length, maximum_dimension_width, maximum_dimension_height. Or one attribute "maximum_dimension" with axis "principle_of_operation" and condition strings like "drop and clear – length"? That seems worse. I'll go with separate attributes per dimension.

Alternatively, use matrix_tables for the two principle-of-operation tables, and also config_level. The schema says matrix_tables preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. These tables partially fit config_level. I think including both matrix_tables (to preserve the structure) and config_level is defensible. But maybe that's duplication. Given the R137 example extracts both matrix_tables AND model_level, duplication is acceptable/encouraged. I'll do both.

Matrix tables:
1. name: "Characteristics — drop and clear principle of operation"
   columns: ["attribute", "length", "width", "height"]
   rows: 
   - {"attribute": "maximum_dimension (max)", "length": "≤ 360 cm", "width": "≤ 240 cm", "height": "≤ 240 cm"} — hmm, values as objects? The schema example shows plain values in rows. I'll keep rows simple: numbers with implied unit in column_units.
   
   Let me structure:
   columns: ["dimension", "maximum_dimension_cm", "minimum_dimension_cm", "scale_interval_cm"]? Actually the table rows are: Maximum dimension (L/W/H), Minimum dimension (L/W/H), Scale interval (L/W/H). Columns: Length, Width, Height.
   
   Better: columns: ["attribute", "length", "width", "height"], column_units: [null, "cm", "cm", "cm"], rows:
   - {"attribute": "maximum_dimension_max", "length": 360, "width": 240, "height": 240}
   - {"attribute": "minimum_dimension_min", "length": 20, "width": 20, "height": 20}
   - {"attribute": "scale_interval_d_min", "length": 2, "width": 2, "height": 2}
   description: "Principle of operation: Drop and clear (footnotes 1,3)"
   footnotes: ["1)", "3)"]

2. Same for stop and go:
   - maximum_dimension_max: 180, 180, 210
   - minimum_dimension_min: 30, 30, 30
   - scale_interval_d_min: 2, 2, 2
   footnotes: ["2)", "3)"]

Actually maybe encode the ≤/≥ semantics: maximum_dimension is an upper limit (max ≤ 360), meaning the max measurable dimension is at most 360? Actually "Maximum dimension: max ≤ 360 cm" means the instrument's maximum measurable dimension is ≤360 cm — i.e., capacity up to 360. So value {min: null, max: 360}. For the matrix rows, plain numbers with a note. I could name the attribute "maximum_dimension_upper_limit". Keep simple: rows with numbers, description clarifies.

Type-level characteristics:
- principle_of_measurement: "reflection of light" (string value)
- measuring_range: "Single interval" — hmm, this is more of a scale-interval structure: single interval. value string "Single interval".
- electromagnetic_environment_class: "E2"
- mechanical_environment_class: "M1"
- climatic_environment_temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, °C
- climatic_environment_humidity: "non-condensing"
- climatic_environment_intended_location: "Closed"
- power_supply_voltage: {min: 100, max: 240}, V
- power_supply_type: "AC"
- power_supply_frequency: {min: 50, max: 60}, Hz
- method_of_operation: "semi-automatic or automatic"
- minimum_spacing_between_successive_objects: {min: 35, max: null}, cm, with description about multiple objects
- software_version: "6.1.r.b" with note

Limitations of use — could be type_level attributes:
- limitation_of_use: "Objects with reflective surface" (all principles)
- limitation_of_use_stop_and_go: "Objects can only be measured correctly when the lowest part of the object or transport material (e.g., pallet) is lower than the forks of the forklift."

Footnotes:
1) With this setting the object is measured on the floor in the field of measurement
2) With this setting the object is measured while being lifted by the forklift. The pallet must be lifted with 5 to 30 cm from the floor. The pallets dimensions are included in the measurement.
3) The multi-dimensional measuring instrument detects automatically the principle of operation.

Recommendation:
- id: "R129" (canonical, not "OIML R 129")
- edition: 2000
- scheme: "A"
- accuracy_classes: not applicable for R129 (no accuracy classes mentioned) — omit.

Test reports:
- NMi-2565570-01, dated 2 July 2024, 50 pages, role: test_report (they say "associated reports" — these are test/evaluation reports). The certificate says "tests and examinations provided in the associated reports". Roles: probably "test_report" for these. Or "type_evaluation_report". For NMi, these are test reports. I'll use "test_report" for the two NMi-2565570 ones and "test_report" for NMi-3927200-01 as well. Hmm, NMi-3927200-01 dated 24 March 2025 with 10 pages — project number matches cert project, likely an evaluation/additional report. Role could be "evaluation_report". I'll use "test_report" for all three or "evaluation_report" for the last. Given ambiguity, I'll use "test_report" for first two and "evaluation_report" for the third? Actually no basis. Let me just use "test_report" for all, since the certificate says "results of tests and examinations provided in the associated reports". Safer: "test_report".

Category: "Multi-dimensional measuring instrument". Keep the capitalization from doc? I'll use "Multi-dimensional measuring instrument".

For config_level values shape: schema says values[]: {condition, value}. Rule 5 says values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. Also footnote markers.

Alternatively encode the whole 3×2 as matrix_tables and use config_level only for minimum_dimension and scale_interval... but those also vary per dimension (min dimension same across dims within a principle: 20 for all; 30 for all). So:
